topics.title: k Math Competition Stories
topics.text:
I know there is a thread for MATHCOUNTS stories, but I also want you to post about your AMC, Mathleague.org/com, ARML, etc, etc experience.



Please tell everyone about your Math Competition Stories!



My storyKindergarten (Yep)Pretty basic part, I went to a private school, pretty easy, so I started homeschooling.


1st gradeI started learning 3rd grade math, and loved homeschooling.


2nd gradeNow this is where is gets interesting. I just started 5th grade math, and I wanted "more". My mother researched some cool math competitions until she found "Mathleague.org". I joined right away as a 3rd grader. I got 1st in the state and 1st in nationals, but I was still nervous. I realized there was a big gap between 3rd and forth, but since I was in 2nd grade, I had 1 more year of being a 3rd grader.


3rd gradeI studied very hard in the usual public school curriculum, but that wasn't enough. I made an account in 2nd grade, but finally joined the community on AoPS in 3rd grade. My mother bought the books, and I started them. I progressed very slowly, but it was worth it. I went strong, back into Mathleague, and, I got the same results of last year.


4th gradeThis year I started Number Theory, and I did the Counting and Probability course here on AoPS. That was very difficult, but it allowed me to be able to solve more questions, getting 1st place in nationals, with a score of 198 (in mathleague). I heard about MATHCOUNTS, but I didn't get what it was. I took the AMC 8 for the first time, and got a 19/25. I also took the AMC 10, and I got... Drumroll... 9/25. :noo:


5th gradeMore recently...



After finishing alcumus, C&P, N&T, and half way through of the algebra and geometry books, I went in strong in mathleague, but I tied for 1st in state, but got 6th in nationals. I was very sad, but I made a challenge to myself that I would score well in MATHCOUNTS. I took the AMC 8 again, and scored 23/25, much better then last year. I took the AMC 10, and got ... Drumroll... 13/25. A huge improvement. At the middle of the year, I travelled through Europe, so I didn't study too much, and I just got back from Egypt in January. (PM if you want details)


6th grade (Current)After arriving from Europe, I realized my math was rusty. I work super hard, and I finished the algebra book. (I'm currently almost done with the geometry). I went into the MATHCOUNTS chapter, and I got 2nd place. I got 2nd place in countdown, and was happy that I made it to state. (I'm homeschooled, btw)



I rigorously took all of the past tests, did intense MATHCOUNTS trainer, and went to state, and I got 32nd. (I live in Texas.)

That's pretty bad, and I was disappointed. I was happy that I got to meet Luke R, and play a game with him.

I'm hoping I'll get top 10 or less in state next year, and I'm continuing to study very hard! (Even though Texas is very hard).



I took the AMC 10 A , and got a score of 114, and I got 3 right on the AIME. I totally failed the B though. :P

I didn't take the 12, but will take it next year.



This year I also finished some basic Calculus...And if you want to know I'm learning Chemistry and Physics (although I'm terrible at both of them)





Please do not spam, or make your story just "Story". Please be considerate to others, and mods/admins please don't lock this thread.

topics.text:
Question. 12 men can reap a field in 25 days. In how many days can 20 men reap the same field.



Solution : clearly, less men will take more days.

And, more men will take less days.

12 men can reap the field in 25 days.

1 man can reap the field in (25 x 12) days

[less men, more days]

20 men can reap the field in  (25 x 12)÷20 days

[more men, less days]

= 15 days

Hence, 20 men can reap the field in 15 days.



My problem :

1 man can reap the field in (25 x 12) days



20 men can reap the field in (25 x 12) ÷ 20 days

A narcissistic number is a number such that its digits raised to powers sum to that number. For example, 153=$1^3+5^3+3^3$.

Rules:

1. Post a new problem with your solution

2. You can use PEMDAS and factorials

3. Make sure your problem actually has a solution

4. Use each digit only once

At the same time, AoPS Prealgebra goes deeper in some areas, and touches on some topics not in BA 5.



For a student that has completed all of BA 5 (including the starred problems), has anyone come up with a recommended subset of AoPS Prealgebra to cover? To celebrate my 1,000th post, I would like to start a small thread where people can post their math counts, AMC series, or any other competition that they have participated in, of their own personal experiences to positively inspire and prepare others that haven't competed yet in the competition in their future.



I do realize that many threads on AoPS talk about people's personal math competition stories, but I hope this one will be more improved. For example, less spam more inspiration!



If you decide to post your story, please make your story using this outline 

[center][code]someone's ____ competition seriescontent
[/code] [/center]

so it's easier for people to read and scroll past.

If someone's story is truely inspirational, give them an upvote and a PM thanking them for using their time to share their story. If you would like to publicly show your appreciation for their impact on your life, you can post in this thread, but make sure it isn't too spamy. :)



Thanks for spending your time to both celebrate my 1,000th post(as I have done a lot of AoPS classes :P) as well as most importantly share your most inspiring math competition stories. :)

~math_is_life_2004

topics.title: Two Logic Questions
topics.text:
1. There is a boat that can only hold a limit of 200 lb. There are 2 kids who weight 100 pounds each, and a dad who weighs 200 pounds. How do you cross the river with the boat and the three people without touching the water?

AnswerThe two kids go, one kid comes back. Then the dad goes, and the kid on the other side comes back. Then the two kids go together.




2. You are in front of a river, and you need one gallon of water, but you have a five gallon bucket and a two gallon bucket. Using only those two buckets, how do you get one gallon of water?

AnswerFill the five gallon bucket with water, then scoop out water with the two gallon bucket. The first time you scoop out water, you will have three gallons of water. The second time you scoop out water, you have one gallon of water.
